01 / motion pipeline

Real frames, not filler.

Four loops are planned below. Generated poster frames are already committed; drop the matching MP4s into website/media/ and the page will HEAD-probe them and autoplay only what exists. WebGL remains the live hero; video is used as material evidence, not a background gimmick.

02 / source audit

Rights before renders.

Adobe Substance 3D Assets and Mixamo allow commercial use inside larger works but restrict standalone redistribution, so they are not downloadable catalogue items here. Poly Haven and Smithsonian stay link-only where API or per-item checks matter. Every other imported row carries a verified SPDX gate.

04 / model index

Primitive-first, then GLB.

The hero object follows the installed threejs-3d-modeler skill: shared materials, named meshes, readable silhouette, metadata in userData, and no heavy imports. The local three.js bundle switches to four committed CC0 GLBs on demand.

05 / live catalogue

8692 rows, indexed.

The browser below reads the same generated payload as the agent surface. Filters are functional; free/OSS-only is the default. Rows expose mode, licence, byte size and source rather than hiding the data behind cards.

06 / hybrid access

Free reads. Paid files.

Illustrative commercial model from the project plan: free read-only agents, permanently free OSS items, per-item licences and subscriptions. Paid downloads remain entitlement-gated by the Worker; no checkout is live yet.
